<!-- Generated by docs-infra Python API -->

```python
vectorize(graph: Graph, axes) -> Graph
```

Part of [`evoxc.transforms`](/api/evoxc/transforms/)

Vectorize a traced graph via per-op batching rules.

## Parameters

- `graph` · `Graph` — a traced `Graph` (the result of `evoxc.trace`). Passing a
  callable/`Defn` raises `TypeError` — for function-side sugar use
  `evoxc.vmap(fn, in_axes=axes)`.

- `axes` — the mapping of graph inputs to mapped axes: an `int`, `None`, or
  a pytree thereof matching the graph's input structure. An `int`
  maps the corresponding tensor input along that leading axis (v1:
  only axis 0); `None` leaves the input unmapped (mandatory for
  static inputs).

## Returns

- `Graph` — A new `Graph` of ordinary ops whose mapped inputs/outputs carry an extra leading dimension (one fresh symbolic dim per pass, named from the active pass depth — `"batch"` at depth 0, `"batch_1"` at depth 1, ... — shared by all mapped inputs of the pass; see `batching._batch_dim`). Unsupported ops — no registered batching rule, control-flow regions in v1 — raise `core.TransformError` naming the op; there is never a Python-loop fallback. `output_tree` and `static_values` are preserved; the input graph is not mutated.

## Example

g = evoxc.trace(fn, TensorSpec((3, 5), evoxc.float32))
batched = evoxc.vectorize(g, 0)          # input (3,5) -> (batch,3,5)
batched = evoxc.vectorize(g, (0, None))  # first input mapped, second not
